approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds molecular graphs from a greedy population of accepted high-scoring molecules using connected-fragment crossover and local atom or bond edits. It builds a fresh surplus pool, then a fingerprint Gaussian process trained on all accepted labels selects evaluations through correlated posterior draws. Its retained identity-admission repair confirms stable canonical keys before pool insertion. Atom replacement currently changes one element at a time; occasional multistep walks can combine substitutions, but there is no direct move that relocates a ring nitrogen while preserving composition.
approach.novelty: Extend the existing atom-replacement menu with one coordinated nitrogen positional exchange: swap a neutral aromatic nitrogen and a hydrogen-bearing aromatic carbon in the same six-member ring. This changes nitrogen placement while retaining formula, connectivity and substituent attachments. The earlier siblings protected carbonyl atoms or whole ring cores, redirected halogen growth, or changed parent allocation. This adds a local alternative without those restrictions. A different lineage exposed only ten such exchanges and missed its score target; here the larger fresh pool and inherited learned selector provide different conditions for testing the same chemical move.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent n-213e85380e04 completes its supplied three-seed panel at macro mean 0.5443738005952443 and population SD 0.013310111166991866. Its actual summaries and run logs show complete valid batches; the accepted trace contains 565 best-parent beats among 4350 generated evaluations. Its identity repair leaves every evaluated molecule and score unchanged, so the chemical neighborhood remains limiting. The source's replace_atom changes one atomic number and may destroy composition before a later edit restores it. A direct aromatic nitrogen positional exchange is absent; this does not claim the entire Parent cannot reach that product through a multistep walk. A read-only enumeration of its 75607 recorded outer-attempt first parents finds 654 of 2125 distinct actually used parent identities with qualifying pairs, covering 21845 first-parent occurrences and 11909 of 41295 mutation-first attempts. Of 7016 sole-replacement pool products, 2079 have an eligible source. The 1940 distinct source/pair applications all sanitize and preserve formula and qualifying-ring aromaticity; 1723 change canonical identity and 217 return the same identity by symmetry. These counts establish available structural moves, not previously unseen or high-scoring alternatives. The carbonyl-protection sibling n-9bee44b1c9c3 preserved its narrow object but lost mean score and still changed adjacent functional groups, motivating a composition-preserving positional edit instead of further blanket protection. In n-abcd951ab7cc, the same exchange family reached ten scored neighbors, with three source improvements and seven losses; its +0.0008412882577690054 paired macro gain missed +0.002. That is mixed prior utility evidence, not an established benefit.
hypothesis: Extend the inherited per-site atom-replacement menu with a direct exchange of a neutral aromatic nitrogen and a hydrogen-bearing aromatic carbon in the same six-member ring, preserving molecular formula and connectivity while changing nitrogen placement.

finding_summary.headline: Nitrogen exchanges reached 30 evaluations and one new task best; mean score rose 0.007397
finding_summary.insights: This establishes a useful local alternative under the existing pool generator and learned selector, including an observed incumbent gain, while narrowing the utility claim to particular molecular families. Pure exchanges were often neutral or harmful, and all eight evaluated descendants that also contained other edits lost to their best generating parent. Evaluated exposure was concentrated in zaleplon, decoration and median; neither DRD2 nor sitagliptin evaluated an exchange. The sitagliptin score gain therefore cannot be credited to a directly scored positional isomer, and the aggregate trajectory difference does not isolate the contribution of each swap. Three later reversals were correctly rejected as duplicates, demonstrating why operation counts alone overstate retained alternatives. Formula and connectivity preservation also leave the larger chemical limitations intact: the successful nitrogen relocation retained a reactive N-F substituent, the overall emitted stream grew in mean size, and explicit stereochemistry remained absent. The evidence supports testing nitrogen position as a local chemical variable; it does not establish broader ring-topology coverage, synthetic feasibility, or a uniformly favorable exchange neighborhood.
finding_summary.results: The intended positional edit executed correctly. All 536 sampled exchanges preserved formula and connectivity; 435 changed molecular identity and 101 were symmetry identities. Changed exchanges reached 404 pool entries and 30 evaluated molecules. Twenty-nine evaluations retained the exact immediate isomer; one also changed another atom later, while retaining the exchanged nitrogen placement and aromatic ring. The 22 evaluations containing only the exchange gave five source improvements, nine ties and eight losses. One pyridyl nitrogen relocation raised an accepted score from 0.438799 to 0.460926 and established a new final task best. Across all three seeds, mean final-best score increased from 0.544374 to 0.551771, a gain of 0.007397 above the registered 0.002 threshold; population standard deviation decreased from 0.013310 to 0.008223. Two seed macros improved and one declined. Zaleplon and sitagliptin task means rose, while decoration, DRD2 and median means fell. Every task completed its budget, all pools filled, and all admitted identities and feedback joins remained consistent. Recorded total wall time rose from 2,391 to 4,705 seconds, with both greater oracle time and substantially larger diagnostic logs.

molecular.headline: Aromatic and ring-rich products include oversized repeats, reactive substituents, short arene bridges and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: All supplied tasks were read, including their Parent trajectories. Each child task contains 900 records, including 870 optimizer proposals. Ring-closure presence ranges from 0.9805 to 0.9908 and aromatic-text presence from 0.9471 to 0.9874; these are fractions of SMILES containing the relevant syntax, not fractions of atoms. The output contains recognizable indole carboxamides, heteroaromatic carbonyl systems, aryl-substituted cyclic amines and complex aza/carbonyl ring assemblies. Across seeds these are distinct families, but leading excerpts repeatedly decorate a limited family within a session. Some products are compact and chemically recognizable; others have repeated aromatic assemblies, unusual heteroatom bonds or severe ring-geometry concerns. Every digest has charged_rate and stereocentre_rate 0.0. Read-only RDKit perception of the supplied SMILES supports the structural descriptions and atom counts below; no synthetic route or three-dimensional feasibility is established by that parsing. Relative to Parent n-213e85380e04, chemistry changes unevenly: one stream grows substantially, another gains cyclic cumulenes, and another contains fewer halogenated products. These are observations of output, not a judgment of mechanism activation.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family consists of medium-sized, alkyl- and methoxy-substituted indole carboxamides connected to pyridyl rings. The first cited product has 25 heavy atoms and three rings, with an indole NH, an amide carbonyl, a pyridyl nitrogen and an N-F bond on the amide. Closely related products change aromatic halogens or nitrogen placement; another high-scoring cited product contains an N-O-Cl appendage on the indole nitrogen. Mean proposal SMILES length is 44.7, ring-closure presence 0.9805, aromatic presence 0.9782 and halogen presence 0.9609. Ordinary aryl carboxamide chemistry is recognizable, but its N-halogen and N-O-Cl variants are less routine synthetic endpoints. The Parent had similar mean length, 44.5, but lower halogen presence, 0.869, and its highest observed record was a bridged carbonyl/heteroaryl assembly at 0.4463521672202675. The child leading family is less topologically elaborate while retaining the same broad aromatic/carbonyl emphasis.
liabilities: N-F on an amide and N-O-Cl on a ring nitrogen are chemically different from ordinary carbon-bound halogens and raise reactivity and handling concerns.

Peripheral variation remains concentrated around one aromatic family; increased aromatic or halogen content alone does not preserve the favorable feature balance, as the duplicated late product shows.
missing_features: The tiny fragments and large repeated-core tail fail to retain the bounded fused-aromatic/carbonyl/heteroaryl arrangement expressed by the leaders.

The highest excerpt offers limited conventional amide N-substitution and alternative core chemistry at the same observed score. Whether removing the reactive substituents can retain that score is unresolved; the data do not identify an additional unseen target pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The supplied initial indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145, while the leading pyridyl N-fluoroamide scores 0.46092619585962435. Within the leading framework, the three cited aromatic F, Cl and Br congeners all receive 0.46092619585962435. The cited alternative pyridyl nitrogen position receives 0.4387992465191 with the rest of that F-bearing framework retained. Thus attachment-relative heteroaromatic nitrogen placement is distinguishable in these observed products, while the particular aromatic halogen is not distinguished in this comparison. Methane receives 0.0, and the late repeated indole/amide assembly receives 9.929836687250678e-11. The visible gradient favors a bounded combination of aromatic surface, carbonyl linkage and heteroaryl placement over fragmentation or wholesale duplication. It does not establish that the chemically unusual N-F bond is generally desirable.

per_task.generated_character: The highest child excerpt contains very large repeated assemblies of aryl and pyridyl rings and conjugated oxygen/nitrogen carbonyl heterocycles. Ethoxy groups, chloromethyl ethers, imine and alkene connectors, cyanates and, in some congeners, aryl nitriles decorate those assemblies. The first two cited products have 91 and 113 heavy atoms, respectively. The final seed-2 excerpt instead contains smaller linked or annulated N-methyl dicarbonyl heterocycles, often bearing N-F, N-Cl or O-Cl groups. Mean proposal SMILES length is 125.3, versus 94.4 in the Parent; child ring and aromatic presence are both 0.9874. This is abundant ring chemistry with substantial repeated-core growth, not broad evidence of ordinary medicinal scaffolds. The complete multi-ring products have difficult synthesis and geometry questions even where their component groups are familiar.
liabilities: Very large repeated aromatic systems create substantial size and synthetic-complexity liabilities; unique strings do not establish useful scaffold breadth.

The leading chloromethyl ethers contain carbon-bound chlorine, while the late O-Cl products contain oxygen-bound chlorine. The leading O-C#N groups are cyanates, distinct from the aryl nitriles present in other cited congeners.
Imine and highly unsaturated connectors, cyanates, chloromethyl ethers, and the late N/O-halogen groups require chemical scrutiny despite their accepted scores.
missing_features: Compact alternative cores retaining the linked heteroaromatic, carbonyl and substituent arrangement are underrepresented in the highest child excerpt, which concentrates on repeated large assemblies.

A chemically coherent version of the useful feature pattern without chloromethyl ethers, cyanates or heteroatom-halogen attachments is not demonstrated at the leading score. The trajectories do not reveal a unique missing decoration or justify a target-specific core.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Methane and the other cited low-end fragments have the observed 0.5 floor. The initial aryl dicarbonyl heterocycle receives 0.548381482770623. A smaller late linked heterocycle receives 0.5775169069797117, and the more elaborate final annulated example receives 0.5974025974025974. The enormous leading assembly receives 0.6114128757484105; a related version without one repeated peripheral carbonyl heterocycle receives 0.6102549646056505. A still larger cited congener receives 0.6112056392805056. These observations favor connected aromatic/carbonyl/heteroatom patterns over tiny fragments but show little score separation among the very large examples. They do not demonstrate that repeated growth itself is useful. The Parent seed-1 peak was 0.6324703199409752 in a much smaller linked heterocyclic family, so the child size increase did not reproduce that observed endpoint.

per_task.generated_character: The leading products combine two substituted aromatic ends, an alkene-containing connector, and a saturated five-member diaza ring. Potentially basic amine centres occur in the ring and side chain; some analogues add an amino substituent to the carbon shared by both ring nitrogens. The leading cited molecule has 31 heavy atoms and three rings. Methoxy, methyl, aryl halogen, chloromethyl and sulfanylmethyl substituents recur. A separate high-scoring seed-0 family has a fused aza/sulfur ring framework with an exocyclic C=S bond to ring sulfur. Mean proposal SMILES length is 65.1, with ring presence 0.9851, aromatic presence 0.9782 and halogen presence 0.9874. The aryl/amine framework is recognizable medicinal chemistry; crowded aminal centres and unusual sulfur environments make the full products less routine. Child and Parent seed-1 and seed-2 trajectories are identical; the strongest diaza-ring family therefore persists unchanged, while seed 0 shifts from the Parent spiro-amine family to the sulfur-containing framework.
liabilities: Some diaza-ring carbons bear an additional amino substituent and are attached to both ring nitrogens, creating crowded aminal-like centres whose stability and accessibility need scrutiny.
Chloromethyl and sulfanylmethyl appendages and the ring-sulfur/exocyclic C=S environment are unusual additions to otherwise recognizable amine frameworks.
All digest charge and stereocentre text rates are zero. Neutral SMILES for potentially basic amines do not establish their actual protonation state during evaluation or in solution.
missing_features: The weak fragments and late truncated/dearomatized products lack the complete aromatic-end/amine/geometry combination that the stronger molecules retain.

The substituted diaza-ring and fused sulfur/amine products have no stereochemical specification. Their spatial alternatives and explicit protonation states are not represented in these emitted strings; a score benefit from representing them is not established.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading aminoalkyl/aryl/diaza-ring product receives 0.9914038363125457. In a close enamine-linked comparison, the N-methyl ring analogue receives 0.981088217863691 and the N-formyl analogue 0.48797702544581545, consistent with sensitivity to amine versus amide electronics in that arrangement. The N-sulfanylmethyl product with an aromatic N-aryl end receives 0.9831131294702842; its late analogue with that aromatic ring replaced by a larger nonaromatic unsaturated ring receives 0.08210159005746291. The final truncated product, losing the other aromatic appendage, receives 0.011495655106721757, and the small halogenated aryl fragment receives 0.001421581552029289. The visible gradient supports the combined aromatic appendages, amine character and connecting geometry. It does not say that every nitrogen or additional halogen independently improves the objective.

per_task.generated_character: Higher-scoring child products are medium-to-large fused and bridged aza/carbonyl assemblies containing ethoxy-substituted aromatic rings, phenyl appendages, N-methyl imide/urea-like carbonyl units, unsaturated connections and, in some congeners, an N,O-acetal centre. The first cited molecule has 33 heavy atoms and five perceived rings, including medium-sized nonaromatic rings. The final seed-2 excerpt contains quinoline-like aromatic groups joined to annulated nitrogen-rich dicarbonyl systems. Mean proposal SMILES length is 56.2, ring presence 0.9908 and aromatic presence 0.9828. Halogen presence is only 0.1379, down from the Parent 0.269. These products carry substantial ring chemistry without depending strongly on halogens, but assembling their connected medium rings and defining their stereochemistry would require deliberate synthetic planning.
liabilities: Fused or bridged medium rings, unsaturated ring junctions and N,O-acetal centres introduce geometry, stereochemical and synthetic-planning concerns.
Serial changes can interconvert amine, amide, imide and urea-like nitrogen environments; ring count alone does not describe those functional changes.
The late duplicated aza-dicarbonyl example adds considerable structural complexity without preserving the score of the better compact arrangement.
missing_features: The low-scoring fragments lack the coupled aromatic, cyclic nitrogen and carbonyl arrangement visible in the stronger products.

The leading excerpt gives limited straightforward alternative ring connections retaining that arrangement, and its stereochemical choices remain unspecified. The observed scores do not identify an unseen target scaffold that can be prescribed.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl dicarbonyl heterocycle receives 0.1678386594791329. The leading ethoxyaryl/phenyl/aza-dicarbonyl assembly receives 0.21361011906838706; its close carbon-for-nitrogen ring analogue receives 0.21301048592169716. That small separation supports neither an indiscriminate nitrogen requirement nor a unique missing atom. Ethane receives 0.012461119656980673. A late doubled aza-dicarbonyl assembly receives 0.16555828159251879, while a more compact bridged relative receives 0.20112987335919708. These are compatible with reward for an integrated aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl arrangement rather than fragments or unlimited repetition. The Parent highest observed record, an alkyl-pyridyl/large aza-carbonyl ring assembly, receives 0.22405709718343647. The child explores different complicated ring connections without showing a simpler leading chemotype.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family links an N-methyl fused dicarbonyl heterocycle to a halogenated arene with a short aliphatic bridge across nonadjacent aromatic positions. The bridge carries a primary amine and fluorinated carbon centres. The first cited product has 27 heavy atoms; its arene bridge contains three aliphatic carbons, while the second cited product has a shorter two-carbon bridge. These are geometrically constrained bridged arenes. Related products carry O-F, N-O-S or N-O-Cl appendages. The later seed-2 family replaces carbonyl functionality with imino and exocyclic fluoroalkene groups and includes N-fluoroaziridines and cyclic cumulenes. Mean proposal SMILES length is 53.9, ring presence 0.9816 and aromatic presence 0.9471. Cumulated-double-bond text presence rises from the Parent 0.0483 to 0.2218. Size stays broadly similar, but unusual ring geometry and bond chemistry are more conspicuous.
liabilities: Very short bridges between nonadjacent aryl positions impose substantial geometric constraints; aromatic SMILES syntax and successful graph parsing do not establish a feasible three-dimensional arene.
O-F, N-O-S/N-O-Cl appendages and an N-fluoroaziridine are reactive or otherwise unusual functional contexts, even when the associated scores are relatively high.

The late examples put cumulated double bonds inside small or medium rings, including a four-member nitrogen-containing ring. This is a ring-geometry concern in addition to the increased cumulated-bond text rate.
The bridge amino/fluoro centres and aziridine substituents create stereochemical choices that the emitted strings leave unspecified.
missing_features: Tiny fragments and large repeated assemblies fail to retain the compact combination of amino functionality, halogenated aromatic surface and polar heterocyclic features visible in the stronger family.

The strongest bridged structures lack evidence of spatially credible, synthetically straightforward ring connections and have no stereochemical specification. Chemically conventional alternatives preserving their useful feature arrangement are underrepresented; no unseen pharmacophore or particular stereoisomer can be inferred from these scores.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The compact bridged primary-amine/fluorinated-arene/dicarbonyl product receives 0.5750908973498792, and the shorter bridged analogue with changed substituents receives 0.5321574883498289. Their simultaneous structural changes prevent assigning the difference to one feature. The cited O-F/N-O-S congener still receives 0.5220117218784629, showing that these liabilities are tolerated in that neighborhood. The very large repeated dicarbonyl/polyaryl product receives 1.6758614448245604e-53, and methanethiol receives 2.449867090426732e-23. A distinct compact imino/fluoroalkene product with an N-fluoroaziridine receives 0.5030795275617259, whereas the cited late cyclic-cumulene examples receive 0.21349359802594703 and 0.2408594025924811. The clearest high-scoring family combines bounded size, amino functionality, halogenated aromatic surface and carbonyls, but the alternative family shows that this is not a demonstrated mandatory group list. Parent seed 1 had a primary-aminomethyl/fluorinated-arene/dicarbonyl peak of 0.5845583988949146; the child moves the amine into a constrained bridge without demonstrating a chemical-quality improvement.

transferable_gaps.evidence: CCc1c(C)cc2[nH]c(C(=O)N(F)c3cccnc3)c(F)c2c1OC receives 0.46092619585962435 with an amide N-F bond. CNC1(F)c2cc(-n3cc4c(c3C)c(=O)n(C)c(=O)n4OS)c(OF)c(c2F)C1F receives 0.5220117218784629 with O-F and N-O-S connections. The observed chemistry can therefore retain unusual bond environments among its higher-scoring products; element presence alone cannot distinguish them from conventional carbon-bound substituents.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently produce conventional functional-group contexts when adding heteroatoms or halogens.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expose chemically coherent local alternatives that retain functional-group roles while changing a substituent. Distinguish carbon-halogen chemistry from direct nitrogen/oxygen-halogen chemistry and from extended heteroatom chains; let the same available feedback compare these alternatives without a task-specific substituent list.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Cn1c(=O)c2cn(-c3cc4c(F)c(c3Cl)C(F)C4(C)N)cc2n(C)c1=O bridges nonadjacent aryl positions through two aliphatic carbons. Cn1c(=N)n(S)c(=CF)c2c(C3C(Cl)N3C3=C=CN3F)n3c4cc(CO)c(cc4O)c3c21 contains a cumulated double bond in a four-member nitrogen-containing ring. One proposal stream has cumulated-double-bond text presence 0.2218, compared with its Parent 0.0483. These are actual outputs despite abundant perceived aromatic and ring chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not reliably respect the geometric constraints of short aromatic bridges and cyclic multiple bonds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support ring construction and rearrangement that account for bridge length, attachment separation, ring size and multiple-bond placement. Retain the ability to explore new topology while making spatially credible alternatives available; canonical identity and aromaticity checks alone do not supply this chemical capability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every supplied digest has stereocentre_rate 0.0. C=C(CNC(CC)c1ccc(OC)c(C)c1)C1(N)N(C)CCN1c1cccc(F)c1F has substituted side-chain and diaza-ring centres, and Cn1c(=O)c2cn(-c3cc4c(F)c(c3Cl)C(F)C(N)(F)C4)cc2n(C)c1=O has substituted amino/fluoro bridge centres. Their strings specify connectivity without choosing the corresponding stereochemical arrangements.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not specify stereochemical alternatives for its substituted saturated and bridged structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve stereochemical information when present and support consistent stereochemical specification when graph changes introduce such choices, with identity handling that distinguishes the resulting isomers. The observed absence is a coverage gap; it does not establish that a particular isomer will improve an objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: C=C(NC(CC)c1ccc(OC)c(C)c1)C1(N)N(C)CCN1c1cccc(F)c1F receives 0.981088217863691, whereas its N-formyl analogue C=C(NC(CC)c1ccc(OC)c(C)c1)C1(N)N(C=O)CCN1c1cccc(F)c1F receives 0.48797702544581545. The late truncated C=C(CNO)C1(N)N(C)CCN1c1cccc(F)c1F receives 0.011495655106721757. Nitrogen presence alone does not retain the favorable combined arrangement.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted chemistry does not consistently preserve a useful combination of aromatic appendages and amine electronics during structural variation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make interpretable alternatives available that can vary core geometry while retaining amine class and connected aromatic appendages, and separately expose deliberate conversions between amines and amides. Use observed feedback to identify valuable combinations instead of assuming that all nitrogen-containing fragments are interchangeable.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One proposal set has mean SMILES length 125.3, versus its Parent 94.4, and its leading repeated aromatic assemblies have very similar observed scores despite markedly different sizes. Elsewhere, CCc1c(C)cc2c(cc(C(=O)NCc3c(C)cc4c(cc(C(=O)Nc5ccc(F)cn5)n4Br)c3C)n2Cl)c1CO receives 9.929836687250678e-11 after repeating an aromatic/amide assembly. Methane, C, also occurs as a zero-score fragment. Neither unlimited growth nor severe fragmentation consistently retains the chemical combinations seen in stronger products.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably maintain coherent molecular size when modifying connected multi-feature structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide structural edits that retain a coherent connected set of functional features without automatically duplicating whole aromatic assemblies or stripping them to tiny fragments. Any size preference should come from general molecular structure and the available feedback, without a fixed formula or size target keyed to an objective.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

retained_mechanisms: Task-local scored molecular-graph population with score-ranked parent sampling across three high-ranked quantiles
Local atom/bond mutation with inner operator retries and occasional multi-step graph walks
Chemical sanitization, canonical/isomeric identity rejection, and graph-based retries for complete novel pools; saturation-dependent retry branches retained but not exercised
Bounded greedy score-ranked survival and subsequent breeding from accepted offspring

Accepted-only task-local fingerprint Gaussian-process archive, exact joint posterior sampling over fresh offspring pools, masked batch selection, and feedback-driven posterior refitting; bounded numerical fallback retained but not exercised

Pool-only stable canonical identity admission with confirmed graph-equivalent alias normalization retaining the original checked molecule and bounded rejection of unresolved representations; this Child exercises four formal non-exchange identity rejections, with no normalization required

Direct same-six-member-aromatic-ring C/N positional exchange appended to the inherited uniformly sampled per-site replacement menu, with formula/count/aromaticity gates, ordinary checking and novelty admission, plus passive index-preserving mutation-sequence receipts
